f09f8628ee9c.title: Power Electronics Control Intern
f09f8628ee9c.description_html:
Company Overview   

Amperesand is reinventing how the world powers its most critical systems.

We are facing a once-in-a-generation opportunity for infrastructure disruption. Electricity demand is skyrocketing, driven by AI factories, electric vehicles, and modern industrial growth. Energy supply is shifting to incorporate a more diverse mix of resources – including solar, gas, and batteries – at a massive scale.

And yet the power infrastructure behind our latest mega-projects hasn’t meaningfully changed in nearly 100 years. Supply chains for today’s infrastructure equipment can’t match the pace and sophistication of critical energy projects. Amperesand is building hardware and software that rewrites this broken power infrastructure playbook to support a new era of energy abundance.

We’ve built a new class of intelligent, software-defined power infrastructure products leveraging a decade of advanced medium voltage Solid State Transformer research that’s now ready for commercial deployment.

Our products and solutions go far beyond the capabilities of traditional electrical equipment. We make power systems that are faster to deploy, dramatically smaller and more efficient, and capable of supporting modern, dynamic energy needs for tomorrow’s most demanding energy consumers.

Scalable in-house advanced manufacturing capability is our foundation for meeting timeline and quality expectation to serve infrastructure customers around the world.

Amperesand is led by breakthrough energy hardware development veterans and funded by top tier investors who share our vision of building a category-defining energy technology company.

With hubs in San Francisco, Reno, and Singapore, our global team is laser focused on building foundational technology to solve the most pressing problems in power infrastructure at scale.

Join us in building the power foundation of the future!

Role Summary 
As a Power Electronics Control Intern, you will contribute to the design, modeling, analysis, and validation of advanced power conversion systems, including AC-DC and DC-DC converters used in low-voltage and medium-voltage applications. This internship provides hands-on exposure to real-world power electronics development, with an emphasis on control systems, system-level behavior, and laboratory validation. You will work closely with experienced power electronics, firmware, and system engineers, contributing through analysis, simulation, implementation support, and experimental evaluation of advanced power converters under technical guidance.

Responsibilities: 

  • Assist in modeling and analysis of power converters and control loops using control-oriented 
    techniques. 
  • Support development and evaluation of control strategies for AC-DC and DC-DC power converters. 
  • Help characterize system behavior, including stability, transient response, and operating limits. 
  • Participate in laboratory testing, debugging, and validation of power electronics hardware. 
  • Support data collection, analysis, and documentation of experimental results. 
  • Collaborate with hardware, firmware, and system engineers on power electronics 
    development tasks. 
  • Contribute to simulation and modeling activities using industry-standard tools. 
  • Follow safe laboratory practices when working with high-voltage and high-power systems. 

Qualifications: 

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field. 
  • Academic coursework or project experience in power electronics, control systems, or related areas. 
  • Basic understanding of power converter operation and control concepts. 
  • Familiarity with control fundamentals such as feedback, stability, and transient response. 
  • Ability to analyze technical problems and learn new concepts quickly. 
  • Willingness to work hands-on in a laboratory environment under supervision. 

Bonus Qualifications:  

  • Coursework or project experience involving power electronics converters or control systems. 
  • Exposure to modeling and simulation tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, or PSIM. 
  • Basic programming experience in C/C++, Python, or MATLAB. 
  • Familiarity with laboratory instrumentation such as oscilloscopes and power supplies. 
  • Interest in advanced power conversion systems (e.g., medium-voltage, multilevel, or SST architectures). 
     

What You Will Learn: 

  • Practical control-oriented modeling and analysis of power converters 
  • Hands-on experience validating control concepts on real hardware. 
  • Exposure to AC-DC and DC-DC converter architectures across LV and MV systems. 
  • How control, hardware, and firmware interact in real-world power electronics systems. 
  • Industry best practices for testing, debugging, and documentation

Please note: This role requires working on-site 5 days a week. We do not offer hybrid or remote options. 

Candidate Confidentiality & Information Protection 

As part of our commitment to protecting confidential and proprietary information, candidates should not disclose or provide Amperesand with any confidential, proprietary, or trade secret information belonging to a current or former employer or any other third party during the application or interview process. 

Please do not submit or present employer-owned source code, schematics, designs, technical documentation, internal presentations, customer information, prototypes, or other confidential materials. Candidates should discuss their experience and accomplishments at an appropriate level and use only information and materials they are authorized to share. 

Pay Disclosure & Benefits

Compensation will be determined based on experience, location, and other factors permitted by law.  

The benefits outlined below apply exclusively to employees located in the United States.

  • Competitive Salary + Incentive Stock Options  
  • Medical, vision, and dental benefits for employees and their dependents, effective from the start of hire 
  • Company paid Basic Life, AD&D, short-term and long-term disability insurance 
  • 401k retirement savings plan through Empower 
  • Employees receive paid time off (PTO), paid sick days, and paid company holidays  
  • Commuter Benefits  
  • 100% paid maternal leave (12 weeks) and paternal leave (6 weeks) 

Singapore-based employees receive benefits in accordance with local government provisions.

Equal Employment Opportunity 

Amperesand is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law. 

Amperesand is also committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your recruiter know if you need an accommodation at any point during the interview process.

f0b7f38a2400.title: Internship: Embedded Software Engineer
f0b7f38a2400.description_html:
About Revel

At Revel, we are revolutionizing the way the world’s most critical hardware is controlled—across aerospace, automotive, energy, and manufacturing sectors. Our next-generation software stack combines an intuitive command/control interface, a specialized programming language tailored for hardware control, and a high-performance runtime environment. We empower engineers to build, test, and deploy critical systems rapidly, reliably, and safely.

 

The Internship

As an Embedded Software Engineering Intern at Revel, you’ll work on the software that connects our high-performance runtime to the physical world.

You’ll work closely with experienced software and embedded engineers to develop systems software, integrate with hardware, and build the foundations that allow Revel to reliably control complex industrial machinery. You’ll gain hands-on experience working across the boundary between software and hardware—from communication protocols and hardware interfaces to Linux systems and low-level debugging.

This is a highly technical internship for students who want to understand what happens below the application layer and build software where performance, reliability, and correctness matter.

You’ll contribute to real engineering projects, learn from senior engineers, and develop experience with the systems programming and hardware integration challenges behind critical software.

 

What You'll Do

  • Write and contribute to Rust code targeting Linux userspace

  • Support the integration of industrial hardware and learn to work with register maps and hardware communication protocols

  • Contribute to Hardware Abstraction Layers (HALs) that allow Revel software to interface with physical hardware

  • Develop software that communicates with sensors, actuators, controllers, and other hardware

  • Learn and use hardware debugging tools such as logic analyzers and oscilloscopes

  • Write tests and contribute to improving the reliability and quality of low-level software

  • Participate in code reviews and collaborate with experienced software and embedded engineers

  • Debug issues across software, operating systems, communication interfaces, and hardware

  • Build an understanding of how reliability and correctness become critical requirements in real-world systems

 

What We're Looking For

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field

  • Rising Junior or Senior graduating in 2027 or 2028

  • Strong programming fundamentals and experience with C, C++, Rust, or another systems-oriented language

  • Foundational understanding of operating systems, computer architecture, or Linux

  • Interest in understanding how software interacts with hardware at a low level

  • Strong analytical and debugging skills

  • Hands-on experience through coursework, personal projects, research, or previous internships

  • Curious, self-directed, and excited to learn from experienced engineers

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, technically challenging environment

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

  • US citizen, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee (ITAR requirement)

 

Bonus Points

  • Coursework or personal projects involving embedded systems, microcontrollers, or firmware

  • Experience with Rust, particularly through personal or academic projects

  • Familiarity with communication protocols such as SPI, I2C, UART, or CAN

  • Experience working with Linux internals, operating systems, or low-level networking

  • Experience with hardware debugging tools such as logic analyzers or oscilloscopes

  • Experience working with sensors, actuators, development boards, or other physical hardware

  • Interest in real-time, safety-critical, or high-reliability systems

  • Experience building projects that bridge software and hardware

  • Experience with robotics, aerospace, automotive, industrial automation, or other hardware-focused applications

 

Why Revel

  • Work on software that controls real hardware — build systems that interact directly with the physical world

  • Go deep technically — work at the intersection of systems programming, hardware, and software

  • Learn from exceptional engineers — work closely with engineers who have built critical software systems

  • Build real things — contribute to production software rather than purely academic or experimental projects

  • Take on meaningful problems — work on technology used by customers across aerospace, automotive, energy, and advanced manufacturing

  • Grow quickly — work in a small, ambitious team where your contributions are visible and your learning curve is steep

 

Internship Details

  • Program: Summer 2027 Internship

  • Duration: June - August 2027

  • Type: Summer, paid internship

  • Location: Los Angeles or San Francisco

  • Work environment: On-site

  • Travel: Occasional travel to customer sites may be required

 

Join us to redefine what’s possible in software for hardware.

 

ITAR Requirements
To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.
